en: Itivuttaka 33 Dukanipāta, Paṭhamavagga Thus it was said by the Blessed One; having said this, the Well-Farer rose from his seat and went into his dwelling. Then, soon after the Blessed One had departed, the venerable Ānanda addressed the bhikkhus: "Friends, bhikkhus! "Friend," those bhikkhus replied to the venerable Ānanda. The venerable Ānanda said this: "Friends, the Blessed One has risen from his seat and gone into his dwelling after saying: 'Bhikkhus, there are these two kinds of persons who appear in the world for the welfare of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the good, welfare, and happiness of devas and humans. What are these two? The Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, and the Tathāgata’s disciple who has attained the destruction of the taints. These, friends, are the two kinds of persons who appear in the world for the welfare of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the good, welfare, and happiness of devas and humans. In this regard, friends, the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, teaches the Dhamma to his disciples out of compassion, having himself realized it through direct knowledge. He teaches the Dhamma that is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with the right meaning and phrasing, and he reveals a holy life that is utterly perfect and pure. And his disciples listen to that Dhamma with eager ears, lend an attentive ear, and apply their whole mind to understand it. Just as, friends, when a rain cloud pours down heavily upon a mountain peak, the water flows down following the inclines;

even so, friends, the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, teaches the Dhamma to his disciples out of compassion... and his disciples listen to that Dhamma with eager ears, lend an attentive ear, and apply their whole mind to understand it. This, friends, is called the first kind of person who appears in the world for the welfare of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the good, welfare, and happiness of devas and humans. Furthermore, friends, the Tathāgata’s disciple who has attained the destruction of the taints teaches the Dhamma to others out of compassion, having himself realized it through direct knowledge. He teaches the Dhamma that is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with the right meaning and phrasing, and he reveals a holy life that is utterly perfect and pure. And his disciples listen to that Dhamma with eager ears, lend an attentive ear, and apply their whole mind to understand it. Just as, friends, when a rain cloud pours down heavily upon a mountain peak, the water flows down following the inclines; even so, friends, the Tathāgata’s disciple who has attained the destruction of the taints teaches the Dhamma to others out of compassion... and his disciples listen to that Dhamma with eager ears, lend an attentive ear, and apply their whole mind to understand it. This, friends, is called the second kind of person who appears in the world for the welfare of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the good, welfare, and happiness of devas and humans. When this was said, the venerable Ānanda asked the bhikkhus: "Friends, what is the cause, what is the reason, why among these two kinds of persons who appear in the world for the welfare of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the good, welfare, and happiness of devas and humans, the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, is declared to be superior? "It is because of the Teacher, friend Ānanda, that the Dhamma is taught; it is because of the Teacher that the Dhamma is proclaimed. The Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, is the originator of this Dhamma, the first to proclaim it, the one who reveals this holy life. Therefore, it is because of the Teacher, friend Ānanda, that among these two kinds of persons who appear in the world for the welfare of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the good, welfare, and happiness of devas and humans, the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, is declared to be superior. When this was said, the venerable Ānanda said to the bhikkhus: "Friends, the Blessed One has risen from his seat and gone into his dwelling after saying: 'Bhikkhus, there are these two kinds of persons who appear in the world for the welfare of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the good, welfare, and happiness of devas and humans. What are these two? The Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, and the Tathāgata’s disciple who has attained the destruction of the taints. These, friends, are the two kinds of persons who appear in the world for the welfare of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the good, welfare, and happiness of devas and humans. In this regard, friends, the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, teaches the Dhamma to his disciples out of compassion... and his disciples listen to that Dhamma with eager ears, lend an attentive ear, and apply their whole mind to understand it. Just as, friends, when a rain cloud pours down heavily upon a mountain peak, the water flows down following the inclines; even so, friends, the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, teaches the Dhamma to his disciples out of compassion... and his disciples listen to that Dhamma with eager ears, lend an attentive ear, and apply their whole mind to understand it. This, friends, is called the first kind of person who appears in the world for the welfare of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the good, welfare, and happiness of devas and humans. Furthermore, friends, the Tathāgata’s disciple who has attained the destruction of the taints teaches the Dhamma to others out of compassion... and his disciples listen to that Dhamma with eager ears, lend an attentive ear, and apply their whole mind to understand it. Just as, friends, when a rain cloud pours down heavily upon a mountain peak, the water flows down following the inclines; even so, friends, the Tathāgata’s disciple who has attained the destruction of the taints teaches the Dhamma to others out of compassion... and his disciples listen to that Dhamma with eager ears, lend an attentive ear, and apply their whole mind to understand it. This, friends, is called the second kind of person who appears in the world for the welfare of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the good, welfare, and happiness of devas and humans. And it was concerning this that the Blessed One, having risen from his seat and gone into his dwelling after saying: ‘Bhikkhus, there are these two kinds of persons who appear in the world for the welfare of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the good, welfare, and happiness of devas and humans,’ spoke thus. When this was said, the bhikkhus were satisfied and delighted in the venerable Ānanda's words.
This was said by the Blessed One, said by the Arahant; thus have I heard:
"Bhikkhus, a person endowed with two qualities is deposited in heaven just as if he were carried there."
Possessing these two qualities, monks, a person is deposited in heaven just as if carried there."
The Blessed One spoke this matter.
the person who is endowed with these two qualities—
"With the breakup of the body, the wise one is reborn in heaven.
This matter was also spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
